_comment: THE USER WAS RIGHT AND THE ENGINE WAS WRONG: THIS BOARD WINS. It needs 158 iterations.
(Renamed 2026-09-11 from edf_co_10_seed9_t4_thin_loop_absent.json, which asserted the
opposite. The rename is the finding, so the old name is recorded here rather than dropped.)
USER, 2026-09-10, on a clicked Combo Off that did not finish: 'Seed 9: Combo Off failure ...
Note that I was later able to Combo off, but it didn't work here.' Their T4 board is four
lands -- Kitchen 1+2 (Overgrowth) = 3, Conservatory 1+1 (Wild Growth) = 2, Conservatory 1,
Mariposa 1 -- with Cloud of Faeries (untaps TWO) and Emiel ({3} a blink), and a Living Wish
ten cards down a 45-card library.
TWO SESSIONS TOLD THEM IT COULD NOT BE DONE, AND BOTH DERIVATIONS WERE CAP-BOUND.
* Session 14c/15b (MTG_COMBO_OFF_BANKABLE): 'a pass refunds 4 against a cost of 3, net +1,
and ApplyBlinkLoop is capped at FlickerMaxIterations = 60, so that loop is worth 60 mana,
total -- while the deck-out alone wants ~100.' Every term of that is correct except the
60, which is not a property of the board.
* Session 19 (MTG_COMBO_OFF_EXACT) went further and called it a PROOF: with the bank as a
(mana, pips) pair, 'fifty pips forces a >= 49, giving 7 + 49x1 + 11x2 = 78 mana against
104. Short under EVERY schedule.' That arithmetic is also right -- and every one of its
three terms is multiplied by k = 60. It proved the board unwinnable IN SIXTY ITERATIONS,
and then the word 'sixty' fell out of the sentence.
With MTG_COMBO_OFF_MAX_ITER (default 400, human play only) the same board is offered, and
the trial apply WINS: 'blink Cloud of Faeries x158 -- COMBO OFF: wins this turn' [WISH-DRAW].
The independent re-derivation this harness runs -- a fresh re-apply through the public
TurnSolver::ApplyPlan, not a re-read of the gate's own flag -- also kills the opponent.
THE LESSON, WRITTEN HERE BECAUSE IT IS WHERE IT WILL BE READ NEXT: a refusal derived from an
engine BUDGET is not a statement about the position. Both sessions called their result a
proof and it was a measurement of the cap. The cap was chosen against the SEARCH's cost, and
the button had been silently paying the search's budget ever since.
ITS OWN NEGATIVE CONTROL, which is what keeps this from being a rule that stopped checking:
CO_ENV='MTG_COMBO_OFF_MAX_ITER=60' bash test/combo_off_check.sh
reproduces the old behaviour exactly -- 'x60 -- COMBO OFF (NOT PROVEN)', apply does not win --
so the fixture fails, and it is the only one that does besides edf_co_26.
The boards that must stay ABSENT are unaffected and still are: edf_co_3 (no {C} source at
all), edf_co_4 (a Displacer whose single {C} the blink itself eats, net_c 0), edf_co_12 (a
two-untap Gorge board that makes no red in the set the untap restores), edf_co_23 (no wish
anywhere in the library), edf_co_25 (no any-colour Aura to dig to). None of those is a budget
refusal -- each is a resource the board does not have at any iteration count, which is
exactly the distinction this fixture's old comment failed to draw.
_library_comment: A Living Wish ten cards down is what makes this fixture REPRODUCE rather than merely pass.
